transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Janelle Rowe (Lumena Head of Data), Dr. Michael Chen (Lumena Director, AI), Priya Singh (Lumena Security)

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros? Samir and I from Redwood — Samir is our solutions engineer who runs the benchmarks and the POC infra.
[00:18] Janelle Rowe: Hi all, Janelle here. I'm leading the data side for Lumena.
[00:22] Dr. Michael Chen: Michael, director of AI, will be helping validate outputs.
[00:26] Priya Singh: Priya on security/compliance.
[00:29] Samir Patel: Great. Today we want to scope the POC: concrete success criteria, workload sizing, what benchmarks we'll run, and the quality evaluation plan — golden prompts, regression, hallucination checks, scoring.

[02:02] Janelle: To set expectations, our primary use-case is clinical triage assistant summaries for incoming patient notes and routing recommendations. These must preserve PHI handling rules but outputs should follow strict format blocks we provide.
[02:21] Priya: Right, and from security side we need full audit logs, KMS integration for keys if we go Private, and us-east-1 data residency for the pilot.
[02:33] Ava: Noted. Redwood has Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options. For POC we usually recommend Dedicated — predictable throughput and isolated GPU pools — but if data residency requires it we can use Private with customer-controlled KMS. Samir, do you want to chime in on infra?
[02:49] Samir: Yeah, Dedicated is easiest to spin up for deterministic benchmarks. We can pin model versions, run consistent tokenization, and collect latency/cost metrics. For Private/On-prem we'd need a slightly longer lead time — maybe 2–3 weeks — to configure network and KMS.

[04:10] Dr. Chen: Let's talk success criteria. For us format compliance is non-negotiable — templates that downstream systems parse. We also care about hallucination — false clinical advice is a blocker. Finally, semantic accuracy: extracting the right intent/diagnosis codes at a high enough precision.
[04:31] Samir: We typically break that into measurable thresholds: format compliance pass rate, hallucination rate, and semantic accuracy score (EM/F1 style depending on task). For routing/classification tasks we can use macro F1; for structured outputs we measure exact-match on required fields.
[04:55] Janelle: Specific targets?
[04:58] Ava: From similar customers we've seen success criteria like: format compliance >= 95%, hallucination incidents <= 2% (per 1k responses), semantic accuracy >= 88% macro F1. Those are starting points — we can adjust.
[05:17] Priya: The hallucination number feels aggressive; what's the definition?
[05:21] Samir: Good question. We'll define hallucination for the POC as generation of clinically actionable claims not supported by the input or explicitly contradicted. For detection we combine reference-based checks against golden outputs and automated heuristics — e.g., entity hallucination detection and unexpected section content. We'll also surface low-confidence tokens via logprobs.

[06:40] Dr. Chen: For semantic scoring: are you using a single metric? We need to ensure it's interpretable.
[06:46] Samir: We'll propose a scoring rubric: for each prompt, compute field-level exact match (EM) for structured fields, token-level F1 for span extraction, and a binary hallucination flag. Then aggregate: weighted score = 0.5 * structured-EM + 0.3 * F1 + 0.2 * (1 - hallucination_rate). This gives a 0-1 score we can threshold. We'll include confidence intervals.

[08:12] Janelle: That weighting seems reasonable. Could we also add format penalty — like if format is invalid, output fails regardless?
[08:18] Ava: Yes, format validation is a hard gate. Any output that fails JSON/schema checks is a fail for that prompt. We'll surface format compliance % separately and treat any non-conforming outputs as candidate failures.

[09:03] Priya: On data privacy: we need logs but redaction — can Redwood redact PHI from logs?
[09:09] Samir: For Hosted we redact certain fields by default; for Dedicated/Private we can configure log retention and redaction rules and integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption. We'll add this to the security docs pack.

[10:05] Janelle: Workload sizing — our expected traffic during the POC is about 20 requests per minute average, spikes up to 150rpm during business hours. Typical prompt length is 350 tokens input, expected output ~200 tokens. Batch size should be tuned to keep p95 latency under 800ms — but we really want <500ms if possible.
[10:31] Samir: Those numbers are helpful. For 150 rpm that's 2.5 requests/second. With 200 output tokens, continuous batching will help cost but may increase latency. For Dedicated we can reserve enough GPU slots to target p95 400–600ms depending on model choice. We'll include a run with optimized batching and one with low-latency settings.

[11:45] Dr. Chen: Which models do you recommend? We are currently evaluating Anthropic Claude and some open models internally. We want a model that balances safety and accuracy.
[11:56] Ava: For this POC, Redwood can run both a high-accuracy open model and a lower-latency distilled variant. We'll provide comparative runs. If you want, we can include Anthropic / OpenAI via connectors for comparison, but that adds variability to cost.

[13:05] Janelle: OK. Now the quality eval plan specifics: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, format checks, scoring approach — what's the deliverable?
[13:15] Samir: Deliverable will be a reproducible eval harness and report. Components: 1) Golden prompt set: you provide ~500 prompts reflecting production; we expect you to mark ~50 as gold-standards with expected outputs. 2) Regression suite: subset of prompts that we run each deploy/rollout to detect quality drift. 3) Automated hallucination detectors and format validators. 4) Scoring scripts that produce per-prompt metrics and aggregated dashboard.

[14:10] Janelle: About the golden set — do we need ground-truth for free-text outputs? Some outputs are summarizations where there isn't a single gold answer.
[14:20] Samir: For freesummary tasks we recommend a two-tier approach: a) golden exacts where possible (structured fields) and b) human-rated references for open summaries. For the latter we'll run an automated semantic similarity metric (e.g., BERTScore) plus a small human annotation sample for calibration. We'll report correlation.

[15:05] Dr. Chen: Hallucination detection for summarization is tricky. What heuristics do you plan?
[15:10] Samir: We'll use entity-level cross-checks (does the model introduce patient ages or meds not present?), contradiction detection against source text (binary classifier), and a fact-checking LLM run restricted to the source. Any flagged item increases hallucination flag. We also surface low logprob spans as suspect.

[16:00] Janelle: Can Redwood integrate our existing unit tests? We have a set of 120 structured validation tests that the downstream parser runs.
[16:06] Ava: Yes, we can run your validator as part of the eval pipeline; you can either run in your environment reading outputs, or we can run it in the POC harness if you provide the validator code as a repo or a Docker image.

[17:20] Priya: Regulatory note: we need auditability for grade decisions. The POC report must include per-request inputs, outputs, model version, and a hash for non-repudiation.
[17:29] Samir: We'll capture per-request metadata including model_id, weights/quantization profile, KV cache behavior, and token-level timing. Hashing and signed logs are supported for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can enable signed logs too.

[18:50] Janelle: Benchmarks — what exact metrics will you deliver?
[18:54] Samir: We'll deliver: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), throughput (req/s), cost per 1k input+output tokens, token generation rate, format compliance %, hallucination rate per 1k responses, semantic accuracy (EM/F1), BERTScore/ROUGE for free text, and regression deltas versus baseline. We'll also provide per-prompt breakdowns and a dashboard link.

[20:05] Dr. Chen: For scoring approach you mentioned a weighted score. Can you include configurable weights? We'll want to tune them after first run.
[20:12] Samir: Absolutely. The scoring scripts take a weight config JSON; by default we propose the earlier weights but we'll iterate with you. We'll produce both raw metric table and composite score.

[21:25] Ava: Timeline for the POC — typical 4-week plan: week 0 onboarding + environment & security signoffs, week 1 golden prompt ingestion + dry-run, week 2 benchmark runs and regression tests, week 3 tuning and re-runs, week 4 evaluation report + decision. Is that aligned?
[21:40] Janelle: That works. We need security signoff in week 0 for KMS and network. Priya will drive.
[21:47] Priya: Yes, I'll review the docs once you share.

[22:30] Janelle: For the golden prompts, do you have a template?
[22:35] Samir: We'll share a CSV template with columns: prompt_id, input_text, expected_output (if available), output_schema (JSONSchema), task_type (structured/text), priority (gold/regression), notes. We'll also share a sample of 50 reference gold prompts to help calibrate.

[23:10] Dr. Chen: What about human labeling? We'll need some annotators for free text scoring. Does Redwood provide that?
[23:17] Ava: We don't provide annotators by default, but we can recommend partners or you can supply a small internal labeling pool. For the POC people we typically label 200 summaries for calibration.

[24:05] Janelle: Regression testing cadence — every deploy or nightly?
[24:09] Samir: For POC we'll run nightly and run a full regression on each canary rollout. The harness supports canary A/B and automatic rollback triggers if composite score drops beyond threshold.

[25:22] Priya: Anything else on format checks? We need strict JSON schema enforcement and escaping rules.
[25:28] Samir: We'll apply JSON schema validation and additional heuristics for dates, codes (ICD-10), and disallowed tokens. Any schema violation counts as format fail.

[26:50] Janelle: How will you measure hallucination rate numerically?
[26:54] Samir: We'll count flagged hallucination events divided by total responses per 1k responses. Flagging uses rule-based checks plus a fact-checker model; we then sample flagged and unflagged items for human review to estimate precision/recall of the detector, and report adjusted hallucination rates with confidence intervals.

[28:10] Dr. Chen: Cost concerns — we'll want cost per 1k tokens and an estimate for production if we scale to 2M tokens/day.
[28:18] Ava: We'll include cost projections based on the POC throughput and per-token costs for the models we test. For Dedicated we can also give reserved capacity pricing to lower unit cost.

[29:05] Janelle: Onboard data flow — we will not send PHI for the POC; we'll send de-identified samples. Later pilot will use real data behind our VPC.
[29:15] Priya: We also need SSO/SAML for console access and RBAC controls for the POC.
[29:20] Samir: We support SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC; we'll include a minimal admin + read-only analyst role for the pilot.

[31:02] Ava: Next deliverables recap: 1) Redwood: POC SOW + pricing, infra and security docs, sample CSV template, sample golden prompts. 2) Lumena: provide 500 sample prompts (de-id) + mark 50 golden prompts, confirm residency/KMS constraints. 3) Schedule first benchmark week of Aug 17.

[32:10] Janelle: Agreed. Anything else on the scoring approach?
[32:14] Dr. Chen: Could we include per-field confidence thresholds? If the model's confidence for a required field is below X, we fail.
[32:21] Samir: Yes, we'll compute calibrated confidence via model logprob and, where applicable, auxiliary classifiers; we'll include per-field thresholds you can tune.

[33:40] Priya: On audit logs, do you provide immutable storage for logs?
[33:44] Samir: For Private we support write-once log buckets and signed audit trails; for Dedicated we can enable long-term retention and signed hashes. We'll share details in the security pack.

[34:50] Janelle: For the regression suite, how many prompts do you recommend?
[34:55] Samir: For nightly regression we usually run 500 prompts (stratified by task) and a smaller smoke of 100 for quick checks. For the POC we'll use your 500 sample set.

[36:10] Dr. Chen: How do we handle ambiguous prompts where human judgment is required?
[36:15] Samir: We'll surface those as 'requires human review' and remove them from pass/fail aggregated metrics, but still report counts and examples. Over time you can expand the gold set to reduce ambiguity.

[37:25] Ava: Anything blocking us from starting the paperwork?
[37:30] Priya: I need to validate whether Private is required for the pilot; if not, Dedicated will be fine. I'll confirm by Aug 12.

[38:05] Janelle: We have one more ask: can Redwood provide an example eval report from a prior healthcare POC (anonymized)?
[38:12] Samir: Yes, we'll share an anonymized report along with dashboards.

[39:00] Ava: Great. We'll send the SOW and security docs. Samir will share the template and sample golden prompts. Janelle/Priya you'll provide samples and confirm residency. We'll tentatively schedule the benchmark week of Aug 17.

[40:05] Dr. Chen: Thanks everyone.
[40:08] Janelle: Thanks.
[40:10] Priya: Thank you.

[44:30] Meeting end: brief chatter and sign-off.

Notes: Transcription contains minor errors and occasional speaker mislabels. Several concepts (KV cache, quantization, Dedicated vs Private) were discussed; Redwood will supply security pack and SOW.
notes: Customer to provide de-identified 500-sample dataset and mark 50 golden prompts. Redwood to run Dedicated benchmarks and provide scoring harness. Security signoff pending.
